name: Explicit time authority
purpose: Own the declared clock domains, bounded current-time acquisition, directed source-to-destination mappings with tolerance, and the distinct regression/overflow/unknown/missing-mapping outcomes.
responsibilities: Accept a finite, host-declared set of clock domains, each with an injected host time source, a monotonic/wall-clock kind, and an explicit inclusive [min,max] timestamp bound.
Acquire bounded current time for a declared domain only; report source failure and out-of-bounds reads distinctly and never fabricate or silently substitute another domain.
Detect monotonic regression in monotonic domains across successive reads and leave the baseline unchanged on a rejected read.
Register directed source-to-destination mappings carrying a signed offset and a maximum admissible tolerance; a reverse direction is never implied.

Convert a source timestamp to the destination domain only through a declared mapping, using checked arithmetic for overflow and a full-range unsigned 64-bit distance computed from the signed ordering of the two values (exact over the entire signed 64-bit domain, maximum UINT64_MAX, never modulo 2^64 and never via a sign bit).
Return distinct deterministic results for unknown clock, source failure, out-of-bounds, regression, overflow, missing mapping, and tolerance failure.

Commit the destination monotonic baseline only after overflow, bounds, and tolerance all pass, within the same critical section; a rejected conversion preserves the baseline and all authority state (SR-015).
state_ownership: Clock-domain table (id, kind, host source, [min,max], last observed reading) bounded by max_domains.
Directed mapping table (source, destination, offset, tolerance) bounded by max_mappings.
All mutable state guarded by a single std::mutex; the authority is non-copyable and non-movable.
interfaces: declare_clock(ClockDomainId, ClockSource, ClockKind, Timestamp min, Timestamp max) -> Result
declare_mapping(ClockDomainId src, ClockDomainId dst, SignedOffset offset, Tolerance) -> Result
convert(ClockDomainId src, ClockDomainId dst, Timestamp value, Timestamp& out) -> Result
concurrency: Internally synchronized with a std::mutex. Concurrent now/convert calls are serialized into a deterministic total order; no data race under ThreadSanitizer.
errors: ClockSourceFailure: host source returned no reading.
ClockOutOfBounds: reading outside the declared inclusive bound.
ClockRegression: reading earlier than the prior reading in a monotonic domain.
ToleranceExceeded: mapped value diverges from destination current time beyond the declared tolerance, where the divergence is the full-range unsigned distance over the signed 64-bit domain.
ClockOverflow: mapped value is not representable in Timestamp.
CapacityExhausted: domain or mapping table is full.
deployment: Compiled in the standalone candidate; the host injects std::function time sources, so no system clock, transport, or external service is opened.
rationale: Centralizing every time decision makes the SR-001..SR-006 cross-domain and regression/overflow guarantees enforceable in one place and keeps raw cross-domain comparison impossible by construction.
